title: Network Protocols and Services
objective: Study-guide review — CISSP — Domain 4: Communication and Network Security: Network Protocols and Services.

items: TCP — Connection-oriented, reliable, three-way handshake (SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK)
UDP — Connectionless, unreliable, faster (no handshake)
IP (IPv4) — 32-bit addresses, connectionless, best-effort delivery
IPv6 — 128-bit addresses, built-in IPsec support, no broadcast
ICMP — Error messaging and diagnostics (ping, traceroute)
Client → SYN → Server
Server → SYN-ACK → Client
Client → ACK → Server

blocks.title: Exam trap
blocks.text: ⚠️ Exam Trap: TCP provides reliability; UDP provides speed. DNS uses BOTH (UDP for queries, TCP for zone transfers). Know the well-known ports (0-1023).

items: DNS — Resolves domain names to IP addresses (port 53)
DHCP — Automatically assigns IP configurations (ports 67/68)
ARP — Resolves IP addresses to MAC addresses (Layer 2)
DNSSEC — Adds authentication to DNS responses (prevents spoofing)
All three are frequent attack targets (DNS poisoning, DHCP starvation, ARP spoofing)

blocks.text: DNS Hierarchy: Root → TLD (.com, .org) → Second-level (example.com) → Subdomain (www.example.com) DNS Record Types:

items: A — IPv4 address mapping
AAAA — IPv6 address mapping
MX — Mail exchange server
CNAME — Canonical name (alias)
PTR — Reverse lookup
SOA — Start of Authority
NS — Name server

blocks.text: DNSSEC adds digital signatures to DNS records, allowing resolvers to verify the authenticity of DNS responses. This prevents DNS cache poisoning attacks.

items: SMTP — Sends email (port 25; port 587 with auth)
POP3 — Retrieves email, downloads and deletes from server (port 110; 995 SSL)
IMAP — Retrieves email, keeps on server, supports folders (port 143; 993 SSL)
S/MIME — Email encryption and digital signatures using PKI
DKIM, SPF, DMARC — Email authentication and anti-spoofing
HTTP — Unencrypted web traffic (port 80)
HTTPS — HTTP over TLS (port 443)
TLS — Provides encryption, integrity, and authentication for web
HSTS — Forces browsers to use HTTPS only
Certificate pinning — Prevents MITM with fraudulent certificates
